I've owned Sony, Canon, and Olympus all in recent memory. I've been shooting with ILCs for about 10 years now, I've used Lightroom, DxO, Capture One Pro, PP, etc. I am not a Pro. I occasionally shoot weddings for friends, or events, not really for pay but for fun. For my own fun I shoot family, landscapes, astro, dogs, wildlife. My workflow has been simplified over the years. I've grown to hate Lightroom's cataloging. I very much wish you could simply turn it off. These days I use DxO 10, I have an input folder on my desktop, and an output folder. I shoot only raw, and I prune as I shoot. I then copy over to the input folder and do a second prune using Irfanview. Once the 2nd prune is done, I fire up DxO. Once in DxO I have a few default settings saved depending on what I was shooting. If there's a specific pic I want to do something with, I take care of it then, or if not, I just crank out the jpgs which head to the output folder. From there, I copy the output over to my home NAS, upload to Amazon, and maybe to Shutterfly. All of this is optimized for speed and effort, as I'm almost always short of time to spend on POST.

If you're looking to do the basics with the software that comes with a system, here's what I've found of the three vendors I've owned:

Sony - Capture One Express if fantastic. I had no problems using it in place of DxO, and actually like the Express version better than Pro.

Canon - DPP 3 was weak, DPP 4 is better, but performing edits and the overall workflow was still rough enough in v4 that I stuck with DxO.

Olympus - Oly Viewer 3 - absolute garbage. Oly doesn't really give you any software worth using.

Depending on your camera model, you may be able to use DxO Optics 8 free:

http://www.dxo.com/us/advancedphotoshop

I'd definitely recommend it over and above DPP if the v8 version supports your camera.
